headline: Search-space constraints and benchmarks for peptide identification in MS proteomics
label: Proteomics Search Benchmarks
summary: Recent proteomics tools benchmark glycopeptide validation and PTM combination scoring while reducing viral search databases by 82-95%.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that peptide and glycopeptide identification is limited by how the candidate space is defined and how assignments are validated. MS Andrea scores combinatorial PTM assignments per PSM using sequence tags in open searches, and the viral proteomics strategy filters sequence databases through single amino acid variant detection, cutting search databases by 82-95% while retaining sensitivity. A benchmark of five glycoproteomics tools on BJAB-K20 data adds diagnostic-ion post-validation as an independent check on glycopeptide assignments. A protein language model study finds that classical sequence methods outperform PLMs for CDR3-based retrieval of antigen-specific receptors, with germline and V-gene context mattering, and the IEDB 2026 update standardizes immune receptor gene nomenclature and CDR delimitation. What is new is the emphasis on constraining the candidate space and validating assignments rather than relying on scoring alone.
